ACE's own AIMS III Phase 1&2 Report states 'The Head of the ASEAN Power Utilities/Authorities (HAPUA) Council appointed the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) as the Implementing Agency (IA)' and 'The AIMS III Report was jointly developed by ACE and the national experts from the ASEAN Member States as part of the AIMS III Working Group, with GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant' [2]. 'The capacity expansion planning task was made with PLEXOS using Energy Exemplar as the simulation tool' [2] -- confirming PLEXOS as the actual tool used to build the AIMS III capacity-expansion model. ACE's own news page independently corroborates that ACE selected and directed GE Energy Consulting as the PLEXOS-running consultant: 'ACE with its selected consultant to lead the works of AIMS III, GE Consortium, wisely welcomed the inputs and feedbacks from all TRG members' [3]. HNEI/GridSTART's own project page confirms ACE itself received hands-on PLEXOS training, but frames it as management-oversight capacity rather than production modeling: 'HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE)...on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study' [1]. ROLE JUDGMENT (8-question evaluator checklist applied): (1) Is PLEXOS named? Yes, explicitly and repeatedly in ACE's own report. (2) Is the org named as doing something specific with it? Yes -- ACE is named as the appointing/directing Implementing Agency that selected and managed the PLEXOS-running consultant (GE Energy Consulting), and procured PLEXOS-proficiency from that consultant via its own RFP (per unresolved_questions.md's prior citation of ACE's 2018 RfP language). (3) Did ACE itself build/operate the production PLEXOS model? No -- the report attributes the actual capacity-expansion PLEXOS simulation work to 'GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant', not to ACE directly; the PLEXOS training ACE personnel received is explicitly scoped to 'project management duties' (i.e. overseeing/reviewing the consultant's work), not independently running production AIMS III simulations. (4) Therefore commissioner (procuring/directing party), not direct_user, is the correct role -- parallel to the ARENA/NERA (ORG-0004) and Energy Community Secretariat/EIHP (ORG-EEUR-0017) precedents already in the master catalogue, where the commissioning body is distinguished from the consultant who actually runs PLEXOS. (5) Second independent evaluator check: the alternative reading (ACE as direct_user, since ACE personnel underwent PLEXOS-specific training and ACE is listed as joint-developer/author of the Report) was considered and rejected because no source states ACE personnel ran the production capacity-expansion/production-cost simulations themselves -- training for 'project management duties' is explicitly narrower than running the model, consistent with the catalogue's qa_reviewer/commissioner distinction elsewhere (cf. EPPEI/ORG-ASIA-0017). (6) Not a duplicate: ACE itself has no prior row in the master catalogue; the only prior ASEAN/AIMS III row (INVESTIGATED-REG-0005) was a REJECTED subject_of_study candidate for the member states collectively, a different organization and a different role question, per this task's explicit framing. (7) Country recorded as Indonesia, ACE's HQ/domicile (Jakarta), consistent with the catalogue convention of recording the commissioning organization's own home country rather than the regional scope of its study. (8) Current: ACE continues in this Implementing Agency/Regional Planning Coordinator role into AIMS III Phase 3 (2024-2025 ASEAN-wide IRRP work), per a 2025 ACE-authored report proposing ACE take on an expanded role as 'custodian of the regional IRRP model' (not independently cited here as PLEXOS-specific evidence since that document describes Phase 3 methodology/governance, not confirmed current PLEXOS operation -- flagged below for future monitoring).
